IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Paging: spike in KV cache churn + continuous-batch failures affecting hosted inference. Alerts: error_rate>5% on /v1/generate, large mem allocs on gpu-nodepool-3. Root ts: 1962104567
Eva: I'm on it. seeing rapid rise in speculative-decoding miss ratio and a lot of draft/target mis-sync logs. linking dashboards: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/kv-cache (tl;dr: write amplification on prefix store)
Sam: grabbing node logs now. suspect continuous-batcher accumulating too many partial drafts, causing large KV writes every 100ms. tail from gpu-nodepool-3: ```2026-03-15T18:02:15Z ERROR kv_store: prefix_evict fail: memory pressure; batch_flush size=4872```
Maria: any customer-facing errors? Jeff, can you confirm support tickets?
Jeff: Two customers reported timeouts and elevated latencies on generation endpoints (us-east). No data corruption reported. We have a couple of 504s surfaced in the last 12m. Notified account teams.
Kai: Looks like speculative decoding forked draft tokens that never deduped in the KV cache due to a race between speculative commit and batch eviction. When batch config allows large in-flight partial drafts, we multiply KV entries. That explains mem spike.
Eva: Action plan: 1) throttle speculative decoding globally (flag flip) 2) reduce continuous-batcher max_batch_tokens and max_batch_time 3) enable aggressive prefix compacting 4) fallback model variant if capacity still bad. I'll run 1+2 now.
Sam: Ready for throttle. Which flag?
Kai: feature.speculative_decoding.enabled = false on runtime-config service. Also patch: batching.max_tokens_per_batch from 65k -> 16k and batching.max_wait_ms 80->30. That should reduce in-flight partials dramatically.
Eva: Applying changes to hosted control plane now (rolling config). Command: ```curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/configs/runtime -d '{"feature.speculative_decoding.enabled":false,"batching.max_tokens_per_batch":16000,"batching.max_wait_ms":30}'``` Doing canary to 10% groups.
OpsBot: Deploy 5583: runtime-config update started -> canary group 1/10 -> success
Sam: Kicking evict compaction job on node gpu-nodepool-3: `/usr/local/bin/kv-compact --prefix drafts --aggressive`
Kai: Also increasing kv_cache.eviction_threshold from 0.7 -> 0.55 for immediate relief. Note: will raise write amplification briefly during compaction.
Maria: Monitoring metrics: speculative_miss_ratio trending down after flag flip. Errors on /v1/generate dropping from 6.2% -> 1.8% in 4m. 95p latency from 2.8s -> 1.1s. Good so far.
Jeff: Customers seeing improvements as well. Support note prepared: "We experienced degraded latencies due to internal cache churn; mitigation applied, no customer data lost; follow-up postmortem forthcoming." Sending to affected accounts.
Eva: Rolling throttle to 100% (global). OpsBot: confirm rollout complete?
OpsBot: Deploy 5583: runtime-config update completed -> all groups -> success
Sam: Post-change logs: no more repeated batch_flush sizes > 1k. Memory pressure on gpu-nodepool-3 down 45%.
Kai: Quick root cause summary for handoff: speculative-decoding produced speculative draft branches that became orphaned when continuous-batcher triggered early flush/evict. Those orphaned prefixes were reinserted rather than deduped, leading to exponential prefix growth under certain sequence distributions (common in streaming-chat workloads). Combined with high max_tokens window it amplified the problem into a cache blowup and perf cliff.
Eva: Outstanding items before next on-call: - run a full pass of prefix dedupe job across all nodes (non-blocking) - add guardrails in runtime to drop speculative drafts if batch pending eviction - add monitoring alert for prefix-count increase (threshold = +200%/5m) - schedule postmortem in incidents channel tomorrow 15:00 UTC
Maria: I'm taking handoff for next shift. I'll run the dedupe job and own the postmortem. Can someone drop the exact dedupe command and where it runs?
Sam: Dedupe run (dry-run first): ```ssh gpu-nodepool-3 'sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kv-dedupe --prefix drafts --mode dry-run --report /tmp/dedupe-report.json'``` Then full run: `--mode apply`. It runs on each node; we'll coordinate a rolling dedupe to avoid CPU spikes.
Kai: I'll open a PR for the runtime guardrails: simple check in speculative path: if batch_eviction_in_flight -> skip speculative insert. Also add opt-in behavior for high-traffic models to keep speculative off by default.
Jeff: Support update sent. Notifying top-10 customers who hit the timeout spikes. Keeping them informed.
Eva: Adding this to incident board: https://tracker.internal/incidents/1962104567. Tagging engineers for postmortem: @Kai @Sam @Maria @Eva @Jeff.
IncidentBot: Incident flagged as SEV2. Time open: 0h 32m.
Maria: Handoff notes to incoming oncall: 1) incident root cause as noted above; 2) mitigation applied (speculative disabled + batching tuned + compaction/dedupe queued); 3) customer impact: elevated latency and 504s for ~20m in us-east, reduced after mitigation; 4) follow-ups: runtime guardrail PR, dedicated integration test for speculative+evict race, add alert for prefix-count, run dedupe sweep; 5) next update: postmortem draft by me EOD.
Eva: Thanks team. If anything regresses ping oncall channel. I'm unassigning now.
Jeff: Closing immediate support loop. Will reopen if customers report further issues.
OpsBot: kube:scale gpu-nodepool-3 replicas 6 -> 8 executed (temporary)
Sam: small scale up helped absorb lingering traffic while config rolled out. Will scale back once dedupe complete.
Kai: One more note for PMs: model teams that rely heavily on speculative drafting (long prefix streaming) should consider recommending lower batch windows for hosted tier or opt into dedicated variants. I'll include that in the postmortem.
Maria: Received handoff. Starting dedupe dry-run now. I'll post progress and attach results to the incident tracker.
Eva: Good job all. Postmortem owners: Maria (lead), Kai (runtime), Sam (infra), Jeff (customer comms).
